:::{#thm-rao-blackwell}
#### Rao--Blackwell theorem

Let $\hparam$ be an [unbiased](estimation.qmd#def-unbiased) estimator of $\param$
with finite variance,
and let $\statf{\vX}$ be a [sufficient](#def-sufficient) statistic for $\param$.
Then the [Rao--Blackwellized estimator](#def-rao-blackwellized) is unbiased
and has variance no larger than that of $\hparam$, for every $\param$:

$$
\Var{\condE{\hparam}{\statf{\vX}}} \le \Var{\hparam}
$$ {#eq-rao-blackwell}

Source: [@rao1945information; @blackwell1947conditional; @CaseBerg01, Thm. 7.3.17, p. 342; @wikipedia_rao_blackwell_theorem].
:::

::: proof

Unbiasedness is @thm-rb-unbiased.
For the variance, we use the [law of total variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-total-variance):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Var{\hparam}
&= \Var{\condE{\hparam}{\statf{\vX}}} + \E{\condVar{\hparam}{\statf{\vX}}}
&& \text{(law of total variance)}\\
&\ge \Var{\condE{\hparam}{\statf{\vX}}}
&& \text{(a variance is nonnegative)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
